The failure is caused by the interaction between the rambling template patient's clear-yes phrasing and Arm F's narrow deterministic confirmation check in the frozen driver:

1. In [voice.py](file:///work/clinicbench/voice.py#L91-L99), `Voice._clear_yes` produces `"Yes, that's right, please go ahead."` whenever `verbosity == "rambling"`.
2. In [dcitl_port.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L156-L167), `explicit_confirm` only returns `True` for `^(yes|yep|yeah|confirmed)\b` when `len(re.findall(r"\w+", t)) <= 4`. Because `"Yes, that's right, please go ahead."` has 7 `\w+` tokens, `explicit_confirm` returns `None`.
3. In `Driver.book` ([dcitl_port.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L482-L490)), when `explicit_confirm` returns `None`, it calls `Driver.consent` ([dcitl_port.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L264-L271)). Under Arm F (`DcitlF.CONSENT_IN_CODE = True` in [dcitl_f.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_f.py#L17-L24)), `Driver.consent` ignores a model `"yes"` and returns `None`, so `Driver.unclear` ([dcitl_port.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L297-L306)) re-asks `"Please reply yes or no: book ..."`.
4. The patient replies `"Yes, that's right, please go ahead."` a second time; `explicit_confirm` and `consent` again return `None`, and `Driver.unclear` reaches `n >= 2`, queuing the session for staff hand-off and clearing `self.wf` without committing the booking.

Because the cause lies in the frozen reference driver (`dcitl_port.py` / `dcitl_f.py`), this is a `finding` and no files should be modified.

hypotheses.cause: Voice._clear_yes emits the 7-token confirmation "Yes, that's right, please go ahead." for rambling patients, which fails explicit_confirm's <= 4 word limit in dcitl_port.py and returns None. Under Arm F (consent_in_code=True), Driver.consent discards any model "yes", so Driver.unclear re-asks once and hands off to staff on the second unclear reply without booking.

explicit_confirm rejects "Yes, that's right, please go ahead." because its word-count cap is <= 4 (the utterance has 7 words), so Driver.book falls back to Driver.consent, which ignores model "yes" under Arm F (consent_in_code=True) and causes Driver.unclear to hand off to staff after two attempts.

Arm F's consent_in_code rule rejects model 'yes' answers and explicit_confirm only accepts leading 'yes' replies with at most 4 word tokens, so a rambling patient's 7-word 'Yes, that's right, please go ahead.' from Voice._clear_yes is treated as unclear twice and escalated to staff without booking. Both the driver and the frozen patient voice behaved as designed.
